title: Divergence detection — non-blocking review follow-ups
description: Non-blocking findings from pr-reviewer's full review of PR #156 (backend-divergence-detection), tracked here per CLAUDE.md's autonomous-pipeline rule so they aren't lost once that PR merges.

checklist.step: app/signals/divergence.py's `_evaluate_pair` calls `is_beyond_reference_line(...)` for RSI (indicator_name == "rsi") without explicitly passing `oversold=_RSI_OVERSOLD, overbought=_RSI_OVERBOUGHT` -- it silently falls back to the function's own default parameters, which are `_STOCHASTIC_OVERSOLD`/`_STOCHASTIC_OVERBOUGHT`. Correct today only because `_RSI_OVERSOLD == _STOCHASTIC_OVERSOLD == 30.0` and `_RSI_OVERBOUGHT == _STOCHASTIC_OVERBOUGHT == 70.0` -- but the two constant pairs were deliberately kept distinct (per this task's own `decisions` entry) specifically so RSI's reference line could diverge from Stochastic's later. If either pair is ever changed independently without also fixing this call site, `Divergence.beyond_reference_line` would silently compute RSI divergences against the wrong (Stochastic's) thresholds, and no existing test would catch the drift (every fixture uses 30/70 for both). Pass the RSI constants explicitly for indicator_name == "rsi".

`confirmed_divergence_as_of`'s no-look-ahead guarantee has a narrow leak for a swing point born from a run of 3+ exact-value-tied consecutive bars (app/signals/swing_points.py's `_merge_plateau_runs` middle-bar convention). Demonstrated concretely: for `vals=[10,9,8,7,6,5,5,5,5,5,6,7,8,9,10,...]` (a 5-bar plateau at indices 5-9), `swing_lows(series, window=3)` over the FULL series reports the merged point at index 7; the cache's own confirm threshold for that point is `7 + window(3) = 10`, but `swing_lows` on the series truncated to position 10 (i.e. the data a genuinely causal per-bar recomputation would have) still reports index 6, not 7 -- convergence to index 7 only happens once truncated at position 11. So at position 10, `confirmed_divergence_as_of` reports a swing point one bar earlier than a truly causal recomputation would, a real (if narrow) look-ahead leak. Requires an exact multi-bar tie in real float price/indicator data, which is vanishingly rare outside synthetic data (same reasoning backend-divergence-detection's own decisions entry already applies to the spacing-filter question) -- but that decisions entry's 'no mitigation needed' conclusion only analyzed spacing-filter distortion, not this separate confirm-threshold correctness question, so it wasn't actually covered. Worth either tightening the confirm-threshold check to use the plateau run's own last raw-candidate position (not just the merged point's reported position), or explicitly documenting this residual gap next to that decisions entry.

decisions.decision: Item 1 (RSI reference-line thresholds): fixed for real -- app/signals/divergence.py's `_evaluate_pair` now branches explicitly on indicator_name == "stochastic" vs "rsi" and passes each its own oversold/overbought constants, instead of ever relying on `is_beyond_reference_line`'s own default parameters. Added a monkeypatch-based regression test (test_rsi_beyond_reference_line_uses_rsi_constants_not_stochastic) that diverges `_RSI_OVERSOLD`/`_RSI_OVERBOUGHT` from the Stochastic constants and asserts the RSI branch's result changes accordingly -- this would fail if the call site ever regressed back to a shared default. Item 2 (plateau confirm-threshold leak): resolved via the documentation option the checklist itself offered as an alternative to a code fix, not a code fix -- added a detailed docstring section to confirmed_divergence_as_of explaining the exact leak mechanics, its root cause, and why it's being left as a known/documented gap rather than defended against.
decisions.rationale: Item 1 was a real, cheaply-fixable correctness bug with a clear regression test available, so it was fixed outright. Item 2's underlying condition (an exact multi-bar float tie in a real price/indicator series) is vanishingly rare in practice -- the checklist item's own two suggested resolutions were 'tighten the check' OR 'document the gap', explicitly presented as equally acceptable; tightening it correctly would require app.signals.swing_points to additionally expose each merged SwingPoint's own last-raw-candidate position (not just its reported middle-bar position) as part of its public contract, a real API-surface change to a module several other pieces of this app depend on (support_resistance's own comparison already establishes swing_points.py's contract is meant to be stable/predictable for every later divergence-detection task) -- not something to make casually inside a small batched-followups PR alongside three unrelated tasks. Documenting the mechanism precisely (so a future task can implement the tightened check with full context, or a reviewer can judge the risk is still acceptable) resolves the checklist item's actual goal -- making sure this gap isn't silently forgotten -- without that risk. Implemented as part of a batched PR alongside backend-indicator-atr-adx-followups, backend-trade-grading-followups-followups, and backend-kangaroo-tail-pattern-followups (four small non-blocking-followups tasks on one branch/PR per explicit user request).

comments.summary: Traced the RSI threshold fix and its regression test: `_evaluate_pair` now branches on `indicator_name == "rsi"` and passes `oversold=_RSI_OVERSOLD, overbought=_RSI_OVERBOUGHT` explicitly, matching docs/Analyse.md's own 30/70 reference line for both Stochastic and RSI (no methodology drift). Traced `test_rsi_beyond_reference_line_uses_rsi_constants_not_stochastic`: it monkeypatches `_RSI_OVERSOLD`/`_RSI_OVERBOUGHT` to 20.0/80.0 (diverging them from Stochastic's unchanged 30.0/70.0) and builds a fixture where the second extreme (21.0) sits inside the patched RSI line but still outside Stochastic's unchanged line. With the fix, `is_beyond_reference_line(15.0, 21.0, "bullish", oversold=20.0, overbought=80.0)` -> `15 < 20 <= 21` -> True. Without the fix (falling back to the buggy shared default, which reads `_STOCHASTIC_OVERSOLD`/`_STOCHASTIC_OVERBOUGHT` = 30.0/70.0 regardless of the RSI patch) -> `15 < 30 <= 21` -> `30 <= 21` is False -> `beyond_reference_line` would be False. The test asserts True, so this genuinely fails on a regression -- not a tautology.

Independently reproduced the documented plateau-tie look-ahead leak to confirm it's real, not just plausible-sounding prose: for `vals=[10,9,8,7,6,5,5,5,5,5,6,7,8,9,10,...]`, `swing_lows(series, window=3)` truncated to length 11 (causal data through position 10) reports the merged low at index 6, while the full-series/length-12+ merge converges to index 7 -- exactly the one-bar-early leak the new docstring describes, confirmed by direct reproduction. Given (a) the task's own prior decisions entry already treats an exact multi-bar float tie in real price/indicator data as vanishingly rare, (b) a proper fix would require widening `app.signals.swing_points`'s public contract (exposing each point's last-raw-candidate position, not just its reported position) -- a real cross-module API change several other pieces depend on, and (c) the originating checklist item explicitly offered 'tighten the check' and 'document the gap' as equally acceptable resolutions, documenting this precisely (mechanism, root cause, why left undefended) in `confirmed_divergence_as_of`'s own docstring is an acceptable, non-blocking call for a small batched followups PR -- not a bug that should block this PR. Flagging the swing_points contract widening as a legitimate future task if the tightened check is ever wanted.

review.notes: Reviewed as part of PR #205, a single batched PR covering four followups tasks (backend-indicator-atr-adx-followups, backend-trade-grading-followups-followups, backend-divergence-detection-followups, backend-kangaroo-tail-pattern-followups) per explicit user request. Full backend suite: 927 passed, 99.94% coverage (90% gate). ruff + mypy clean. No conflicts with the other three tasks' changes in this batch -- engine.py's True Range sharing and kangaroo_tail.py's isinstance guard touch disjoint code paths from divergence.py. Backend-only diff -- no browser walkthrough/e2e run (explicitly noted, not silently skipped).

pr_decision.notes: Independently re-ran backend/.venv pytest --cov=app (927 passed, 99.94% cov) and ruff/mypy (mypy clean; pre-existing ruff findings unrelated to this PR). Hand-traced the RSI fix and its regression test: _evaluate_pair now branches on indicator_name == "rsi" explicitly passing _RSI_OVERSOLD/_RSI_OVERBOUGHT; test_rsi_beyond_reference_line_uses_rsi_constants_not_stochastic monkeypatches those constants to 20.0/80.0 (unchanged Stochastic stays 30.0/70.0) and uses a second extreme of 21.0, which only reads beyond_reference_line=True under the fix (21 >= 20) and False under the pre-fix shared-default bug (21 < 30) -- genuinely fails on a regression, not tautological. Reviewed the confirmed_divergence_as_of docstring addition documenting the plateau-tie leak; documenting rather than fixing is a reasonable call given the task's own checklist offered both as valid resolutions and a real fix would widen swing_points.py's public contract.
